review_notes: I read the whole target file and searched the `lean/` tree for downstream uses of `factorRadiusLevel`, `factorSwitchList` and `actualFactorStops`. I found one problem: `factorRadiusLevel` has no evaluation lemmas, so every caller has to unfold its `if` chain with its own simp set. The finding below gives the evidence. Things I checked and did not report: (1) The `factorSwitchList_*` membership lemmas are only passed as terms to other lemmas in MultipointActualExpectation.lean, never used by simp. A simp-normal `mem_factorSwitchList` iff lemma would therefore not help any existing use. (2) The right-hand side of `actual_phase_switch_clock` is also an `if k = 0 … else if k = 1 …` chain. The one caller with a concrete `k` closes it with `simpa only [ite_true]`, which works. Restating it with `factorRadiusLevel` would bring in a `ring` step for k=1, because `(u₀+u₂)/2 - u₀` and `(u₂-u₀)/2` are not syntactically equal. So I did not report it as a clear improvement. (3) No `@[simp]` attributes appear in the file, so there are no competing rules or loops to assess. I did not run Lean, so I have not checked that the proposed `by simp [factorRadiusLevel]` proofs compile, though they are routine.

findings.excerpt: if k = 0 then u₀ else if k = 1 then (u₀+u₂)/2 else u₂
findings.problem: `factorRadiusLevel` is defined as a nested `if` on `Fin 3`, and the file gives no equation lemmas for the three concrete indices. So every proof that meets `factorRadiusLevel u₀ u₂ 2` (or `0`, or `1`) has to unfold the definition and then discharge the `Fin` decidable equalities with whatever simp set it happens to choose. The uses show this happening. The target file runs `norm_num [factorRadiusLevel]` three times (lines 21, 26, 157). MultipointCompletionExhaustion.lean proves a one-off `hfactor` with `norm_num [factorRadiusLevel]`. MultipointActualBudget.lean needs `simp only [ρ, actualFactorStops, factorRadiusLevel, Fin.reduceEq, ite_false, cutoffStop]`. The normal forms we want are `u₀`, `(u₀+u₂)/2` and `u₂`, but they can only be reached by unfolding the whole `if` chain.
findings.proposed_change:
Add three evaluation lemmas right after the definition:
```
@[simp] lemma factorRadiusLevel_zero (u₀ u₂ : ℝ) : factorRadiusLevel u₀ u₂ 0 = u₀ := by
  simp [factorRadiusLevel]
@[simp] lemma factorRadiusLevel_one (u₀ u₂ : ℝ) : factorRadiusLevel u₀ u₂ 1 = (u₀+u₂)/2 := by
  simp [factorRadiusLevel]
@[simp] lemma factorRadiusLevel_two (u₀ u₂ : ℝ) : factorRadiusLevel u₀ u₂ 2 = u₂ := by
  simp [factorRadiusLevel]
```
Then replace the ad hoc unfoldings: `hfactor` in MultipointCompletionExhaustion becomes `factorRadiusLevel_two _ _`, or simply `simp only [factorRadiusLevel_two]`. In MultipointActualBudget, replace `factorRadiusLevel, Fin.reduceEq, ite_false` with `factorRadiusLevel_two`. The `fin_cases k <;> norm_num [factorRadiusLevel]` proofs can use `simp`/`norm_num` directly, because after `fin_cases` the indices are literals.
findings.benefit: With these lemmas, concrete indices simplify straight to their canonical values. Callers no longer depend on the `if` encoding of the definition or have to add `Fin.reduceEq`/`ite_false` to their simp sets. The downstream proofs get shorter and do not break if the definition is later restated, for example with `![u₀, (u₀+u₂)/2, u₂]` or a `match`. The lemmas assume nothing and only rewrite a closed literal index, so they cannot cause a simp loop.
